_meta.indication: Reduction of elevated intraocular pressure (IOP) in patients with open-angle glaucoma or ocular hypertension.

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-masked, active-controlled, parallel-group, multicenter non-inferiority study of DE-117 0.002% QD vs timolol 0.5% BID over a 3-month double-masked treatment period.
pivotal_trials.population: Subjects with open-angle glaucoma (OAG) or ocular hypertension (OHT)
pivotal_trials.endpoint: IOP in the study eye at each of 9 scheduled timepoints (08:00, 10:00, and 16:00 hrs at Week 1, Week 6, and Month 3)
pivotal_trials.result: Met non-inferiority: upper limits of the 95% CIs for the mean IOP difference were <1.5 mmHg at all 9 timepoints (statistical criteria) and did not exceed 1.0 mmHg at the majority of timepoints (clinical criteria).

nct_ctgov.title: A Phase III Study Assessing the Efficacy and Safety of DE-117 Ophthalmic Solution Compared With Timolol Maleate Ophthalmic Solution 0.5% in Subjects With Glaucoma or Ocular Hypertension - Spectrum 4 Study

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, masked, active-controlled, parallel-group, multinational study of DE-117 0.002% QD vs latanoprost 0.005% QD, with a 3-month treatment period, in Asia.
pivotal_trials.population: Subjects with open-angle glaucoma (OAG) or ocular hypertension (OHT), conducted in Asia (India, Taiwan, Korea, Singapore)
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Mean diurnal IOP at Month 3 (average of IOP at 3 time points: 09:00, 13:00, and 17:00 hrs)
pivotal_trials.result: Met non-inferiority to latanoprost: upper limits of the 95% CIs for the mean IOP difference were <1.5 mmHg at all measurement times.

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-masked, active-controlled, parallel-group, multicenter non-inferiority study of DE-117 0.002% QD vs timolol 0.5% BID over a 3-month double-masked treatment period, with a 9-month open-label safety extension.
pivotal_trials.population: Subjects with open-angle glaucoma (OAG) or ocular hypertension (OHT)
pivotal_trials.endpoint: IOP in the study eye at each of 9 scheduled timepoints (08:00, 10:00, and 16:00 hrs at Week 1, Week 6, and Month 3)
pivotal_trials.result: Did not meet non-inferiority: the upper limit of the 95% CI for the treatment difference exceeded 1.5 mmHg for 3 of the 9 timepoints, so DE-117 did not demonstrate non-inferiority to timolol.

nct_ctgov.title: A Phase III Study Assessing the Efficacy and Safety of DE-117 Ophthalmic Solution Compared With Timolol Maleate Ophthalmic Solution 0.5% in Subjects With Glaucoma or Ocular Hypertension - Spectrum 3 Study

key_safety: Data reflect exposure in 600 patients for up to 3 months. Most common adverse reactions (incidence ≥1%): conjunctival hyperemia (9%), photophobia (5%), vision blurred (4%), dry eye (3%), instillation site pain (3%), eye pain (2%), ocular hyperemia (2%), punctate keratitis (2%), headache (2%), eye irritation (1%), and visual impairment (1%).
target_moa: Omidenepag isopropyl is a prodrug of omidenepag, a relatively selective prostaglandin E2 (EP2) receptor agonist that decreases intraocular pressure.
modality: Small molecule (topical ophthalmic prostaglandin EP2 receptor agonist, administered as an isopropyl-ester prodrug)

advisory_committee.vote: No Advisory Committee Meeting was required or convened for this NDA.

summary.text: Standard 505(b) NDA supported by three Phase 3 active-controlled non-inferiority studies; no accelerated approval or expedited-program designations were noted. FDA issued a November 9, 2021 complete-response/action letter based on manufacturing facility deficiencies; the applicant submitted a May 6, 2022 amendment (Class 2 resubmission) and the NDA was approved in the second review cycle with a required corneal-endothelial-cell postmarketing trial.

requirement.text: 4339-1: Conduct a randomized, controlled trial to evaluate corneal endothelial health (number/density of corneal endothelial cells by specular microscopy at baseline and over at least one year) in at least 100 patients receiving omidenepag isopropyl ophthalmic solution.
